newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel off sharply on political scandal.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel off sharply on political scandal.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened sharply on Thursday as political uncertainty prompted strong demand for the dollar, dealers said.
In the early morning the dollar was trading as high as 3.42 shekels, against Wednesday's representative rate of 3.398, before falling back slightly to 3.41.

"We see a rise (in the dollar) of half a percent, three quarters of a percent. It's because of the political uncertainty. People are selling shekels and buying dollars, there is a fear that maybe foreign investors will flee," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
President Benjamin Netanyahu is fighting for his political life after police said on Wednesday he should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal.
It is not yet clear whether Netanyahu would be charged or forced to resign in the scandal over a political appointment.
A dealer at Bank Hapoalim said he did not believe the shekel would remain this weak in coming days unless interest rates decline.
When asked what would happen if the government fell, the dealer said: "If the government falls then we will have more important things to worry about than the shekel-dollar rate."
